references.text: The account of the days of Noah in [ref:1 Mos 6:1-8|Genesis 6:1-8], where humanity's wickedness is described before the flood. Jesus refers directly to "the days of Noah" as a picture of the condition before the coming of the Son of Man.

The flood account itself in [ref:1 Mos 7:6-24|Genesis 7:6-24] describes how judgment came suddenly upon people while they were living their daily lives – exactly the point Jesus makes in his comparison.

The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 24:37-39|Matthew 24:37-39] where Jesus uses the same comparison with the days of Noah and expands on it: people ate, drank, and married right up until the flood came and took them all. The same teaching about the unexpected coming of the Son of Man.

In [ref:2 Pet 2:5|2 Peter 2:5] Noah is called "a preacher of righteousness" and how God did not spare the ancient world but preserved Noah when He brought the flood upon the ungodly – an example of sudden judgment.

[ref:2 Pet 3:3-7|2 Peter 3:3-7] draws a parallel between Noah's flood and the coming judgment, warning against scoffers who in the last days will deny the Lord's coming, just as people in Noah's days ignored the coming judgment.

[ref:Hebr 11:7|Hebrews 11:7] mentions Noah's faith: he was warned about what was not yet seen and built the ark, and by that he condemned the world. This highlights the contrast between Noah and those who were unprepared.

[ref:1 Pet 3:20|1 Peter 3:20] refers to the days of Noah when God's patience waited while the ark was being built, and only eight souls were saved through water – a picture of the few who are prepared when judgment comes.

[ref:Luk 17:28-30|Luke 17:28-30] continues with a similar comparison to the days of Lot, reinforcing the point: daily life went on right up until judgment suddenly struck, just as it will be on the day the Son of Man is revealed.

[ref:Luk 21:34-36|Luke 21:34-36] warns against letting your hearts be weighed down by carousing, drunkenness, and the worries of life, so that the day comes suddenly upon you – an exhortation that expands on the picture of unpreparedness in Noah's days.
